segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Hi Dana, yeah, thanks for making time. I wanted to walk through the revised quote for 42 seats and make sure the start date and billing terms line up with what you need.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yep, that works. I have it open. The seat count is right for the initial rollout, but we may add the finance team later, maybe another 8 users in Q2.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. So the quote is for 42 seats at $68 per user per month, annual term, with a February 1 start date. If you add the 8 later, we would just co-term those to the same renewal date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And the invoice would be one annual invoice up front, correct?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct. Total is $34,272 before tax for the year. I also included the implementation package at $4,500, one time, based on the two workflow templates and the admin training.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That matches what we discussed. On implementation, can you still support a go-live by March 15? Our team wants to stop using the shared spreadsheets before month-end close.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, March 15 is reasonable if we can get the kickoff done the week of February 5. We’d need your field mapping file and sample exports from the billing tool by February 9.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That should be fine. Legal had one question on the auto-renewal language. They’re asking for 30 days’ notice instead of 60.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: I can send that to deal desk today. We’ve approved 30 days on similar annual agreements, so I don’t expect that to be an issue.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. If you can send the updated order form with that change, I’ll route it for signature. We’re trying to have it done by next Wednesday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Perfect. I’ll update the terms, confirm the co-term language for future seats, and send the order form this afternoon.
